newsitem.title: USA: IBM R&D accounting boost net 10 pct - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: IBM R&D accounting boost net 10 pct - Barron's.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp's earnings benefit by as much as 10 percent from the use of a standard accounting write-off for "in process" research and development, Barron's reported in its December 23 issue.

Abraham Briloff, a professor of accounting and ethics at Binghamton Univerity, takes issue with what he acknowledges is a widespread practice among high-technology companies, and one mandated under U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.
The professor wrote that "a not-insignificant portion of the earnings to which IBM's fans now attach a growth multiple aren't economic profits at all, but mere accounting chimera."

The article criticizes what it calls "obscure accounting rules" that have allowed companies to take a "big bath up front," boosting future earnings reports. He uses IBM's accounting for its Lotus acquisition as a case in point.

In the Barron's article, Briloff computed this practice of writing off software acquisitions has benefited IBM to the tune of $401 million, after-tax, or 10 percent of IBM's $3.84 billion in net earnings for the first nine months of 1996.
